bucket: Building Envelope: Insulation, Air Sealing & Roofs

census.bucket: Building Envelope: Insulation, Air Sealing & Roofs

variations.name: Cellulose and recycled-content insulation
variations.description: Loose-fill, dense-pack and batt insulation made from recycled paper, cardboard or textiles stores carbon, has very low embodied energy, and is already cost-competitive with fiberglass for attics and retrofit wall fills.

companies.name: Greenfiber
companies.what: Largest North American cellulose insulation manufacturer; blow-in and dense-pack products made from ~85% recycled paper fiber (SANCTUARY brand).
companies.signal: Multi-plant national footprint with big-box retail distribution.

companies.name: CleanFiber
companies.what: Makes cellulose insulation from recycled corrugated cardboard instead of dwindling newsprint, yielding lower dust and more consistent product.
companies.signal: $33M Series B (Spring Lane Capital) plus $20M DOE MESC grant and $10M 48C tax credit in 2024 (>$75M total); Buffalo plant operating with new plants planned in WA, TX, AZ, MI; ranked #1 manufacturer on 2024 Inc. 5000.

companies.name: Nu-Wool
companies.what: Family-owned Michigan cellulose maker (since 1949) producing high-recycled-content wall and attic insulation with a certified installer network.
companies.signal: Long-established regional brand in US Midwest/East.

companies.name: Bonded Logic
companies.what: UltraTouch batts made from post-consumer recycled denim and cotton fiber, marketed as itch-free and safe to handle.
companies.signal: Longtime niche player sold through national retail channels.

companies.name: isofloc
companies.what: European supplier of cellulose blow-in insulation systems plus the installation machinery and installer training behind them.
companies.signal: Deployed for decades across DACH and wider Europe.

variations.name: Wood-fiber insulation
variations.description: Batts, rigid boards and loose-fill made from softwood residuals offer fiberglass-class R-values with carbon storage and vapor-open performance, and are moving from a mature European niche into North America.

companies.name: TimberHP (GO Lab)
companies.what: Only North American producer of wood-fiber batts, boards and loose-fill, made in a converted Maine paper mill.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 in March 2025 after >$30M construction overruns; emerged in 77 days (June 2025) with BlackRock-led bondholders converting debt to equity plus ~$29M new financing; TimberBoard rigid line now rolling out.

companies.name: Steico
companies.what: World's largest wood-fibre insulation producer (flexible batts, rigid boards, I-joists) with 27 production lines in Poland and France.
companies.signal: Kingspan completed its €251M purchase of a 51% stake in January 2024; demand tied to EU renovation wave.

companies.name: Gutex
companies.what: Black Forest wood-fibre boardmaker; new Eschbach plant with drying capacity up to 4,800 m³/day for renders, sarking and cavity boards.
companies.signal: Family-owned; major capacity expansion came online 2023-24.

companies.name: Soprema (Pavatex)
companies.what: French waterproofing/roofing group that produces Pavatex wood-fibre insulation boards within its envelope portfolio.
companies.signal: Pavatex integrated since 2016 with pan-European distribution.

variations.white_space: North America has exactly one producer (TimberHP), and its Chapter 11 shows the capital intensity of mill conversions; as codes start counting embodied carbon, a second NA plant or low-cost import channel is an obvious opening.

variations.name: Hemp, straw, sheep's wool, mycelium and other bio-based insulation
variations.description: Fast-growing fibers and fungal composites turn agricultural byproducts into carbon-storing batts, blocks and panels; hemp, straw and wool are commercially sold while mycelium remains pilot-stage.

companies.name: Hempitecture
companies.what: US manufacturer of HempWool batts and PlantPanel rigid continuous insulation at its Jerome, Idaho plant.
companies.signal: $8.42M DOE award for a second plant in Tennessee; >$6M equity crowdfunding in 2025; PlantPanel launched 2025 under new ICC-ES natural-fiber standards.

companies.name: EcoCocon
companies.what: Prefabricated structural straw-and-timber wall panels (98% bio-based) certified by the Passive House Institute.
companies.signal: Panels shipped to 30+ countries from Slovak production.

companies.name: IsoHemp
companies.what: Belgian maker of hemp-lime masonry blocks for insulating, vapor-open envelope walls.
companies.signal: Automated Fernelmont plant with multi-million-block annual capacity.

companies.name: HempFlax Building Solutions
companies.what: Vertically integrated European hemp grower/processor producing hemp-fiber insulation (Thermo Natur lines).
companies.signal: Operating since 1993 across NL/DE/RO.

companies.name: Havelock Wool
companies.what: Reno-based maker of sheep's-wool batts and blow-in from New Zealand wool with no chemical binders.
companies.signal: National rollout via The Home Depot online announced December 2025; scaling production.

companies.name: Mykor
companies.what: Bristol/Lisbon startup growing MykoFoam, a carbon-negative mycelium insulation panel from industrial cellulosic waste.
companies.signal: €4.6M raised (~4x prior funding); Portuguese pilot plant; product in regulatory review for commercial deployment.

companies.name: Biohm
companies.what: London mycelium-insulation developer that grew panels from food and agricultural waste streams.
companies.signal: Raised £6.6M Series A (Formica Capital) but failed to reach scale; UK Companies House lists the company as 'In Administration'.

companies.name: Ecovative
companies.what: Mycelium-materials pioneer (15+ years) whose MycoComposite platform spawned insulation experiments; today focused mainly on packaging and foam alternatives.
companies.signal: Category pioneer; insulation remains a side application.

companies.name: GROWN.bio
companies.what: Dutch producer of mycelium-based panels, acoustic products and small-batch insulation.
companies.signal: Small-scale EU operations.

variations.white_space: Bio-based materials are commercial but a rounding error of the insulation market — fragmented feedstock supply, code approvals and fire/moisture certification keep installed costs high, and Biohm's administration shows the cash-burn risk in mycelium. The opening is code-listed, price-competitive bio-based product in mainstream channels; Hempitecture's DOE-backed Tennessee plant and Havelock's Home Depot listing are the first moves.

variations.name: Aerogel and vacuum-insulated panels for space-constrained retrofits
variations.description: Silica aerogels and vacuum panels deliver 2-10x the R-value per inch of conventional insulation, letting thin walls, terraces and historic facades be insulated where thickness is impossible — at a steep price premium.

companies.name: Aspen Aerogels
companies.what: Category leader in silica-aerogel blanket insulation (Spaceloft for buildings; Pyrogel/Cryogel industrial); buildings is a niche line beside its EV thermal-barrier business.
companies.signal: NYSE: ASPN with ~$450M FY2024 revenue, mostly PyroThin EV barriers and energy-industrial.

companies.name: Armacell
companies.what: Global flexible-foam insulation maker producing ArmaGel aerogel blankets for thin, high-R industrial and building applications.
companies.signal: Established global manufacturer with dedicated aerogel lines.

companies.name: Cabot Corporation
companies.what: Produces particulate silica aerogel (Lumira/Enova) used in insulating daylighting panels, plasters and coatings.
companies.signal: Commercial aerogel production near Frankfurt since 2003.

companies.name: va-Q-tec
companies.what: Leading vacuum-insulation-panel (VIP) maker for buildings, appliances and cold chain.
companies.signal: Taken private by EQT X and delisted from Frankfurt in August 2023; pharma container business merged into Envirotainer in 2024 while VIP products continue as va-Q-tec Thermal Solutions.

companies.name: Kingspan
companies.what: OPTIM-R vacuum insulated panels giving ultra-thin R performance for balconies, terraces and space-constrained retrofits.
companies.signal: Multi-billion-euro global insulation leader.

companies.name: KrossLinker
companies.what: Singapore deep-tech startup with a low-cost, water-based aerogel manufacturing process (Cryar boards), targeting cold chain and building efficiency.
companies.signal: Seed-funded (~$1.3M; Seeds Capital, ADB Ventures); opened Series A.

companies.name: AeroShield Materials
companies.what: MIT spinout making transparent silica-aerogel sheets that roughly double window/glazing insulation value.
companies.signal: $14.5M ARPA-E SCALEUP award; pilot manufacturing facility opened in Waltham, MA in 2024.

variations.white_space: Cost-per-R remains 5-10x bulk insulation, confining aerogel and VIPs to niches; cracking low-cost ambient-pressure aerogel drying (KrossLinker's bet) or VIP edge-loss and puncture durability would open thin-wall urban retrofit at scale.

variations.name: Low-GWP spray foams (HFO-blown) and cavity-fill alternatives
variations.description: Closed-cell spray polyurethane delivers high R-per-inch plus air sealing, and the switch from HFC to HFO blowing agents (GWP ~1 vs ~700+) removed most of its lifecycle climate penalty.

companies.name: Huntsman Building Solutions
companies.what: Heatlok HFO closed-cell foams using Honeywell Solstice blowing agent (GWP 1), including high-lift single-pass R-49 products.
companies.signal: Formed 2020 from Demilec and Icynene-Lapolla acquisitions; one of the world's largest spray-foam platforms.

companies.name: Carlisle Spray Foam Insulation
companies.what: SealTite PRO HFO second-generation low-GWP closed-cell foam for residential and commercial cavities.
companies.signal: Part of Carlisle Companies' (NYSE: CSL) building-envelope portfolio.

companies.name: Natural Polymers (Owens Corning)
companies.what: Cortland, IL spray-foam maker whose Natural-Therm 2.0 HFO uses Chemours Opteon blowing agent with GWP <2.
companies.signal: Acquired by Owens Corning in 2022 to enter spray foam.

companies.name: BASF
companies.what: Global SPF and rigid polyurethane supplier converting product lines (Walltite/Spraytite) to HFO chemistry.
companies.signal: Chemical major with worldwide foam systems business.

companies.name: Honeywell
companies.what: Solstice LBA hydrofluoroolefin blowing agent (GWP ~1) that enabled the industry-wide low-GWP foam transition.
companies.signal: Solstice is a >$1B product franchise across refrigerants and blowing agents.

companies.name: Chemours
companies.what: Opteon 1100 low-GWP blowing agent supplied to foam formulators including Natural Polymers.
companies.signal: One of two dominant HFO blowing-agent suppliers.

variations.name: Air-sealing technology: aerosolized envelope/duct sealing and membrane/tape systems
variations.description: Air leakage drives 25-40% of heating/cooling loads; aerosolized sealants plug leaks from inside ducts and whole envelopes in hours, while tapes, smart membranes and integrated sheathing achieve airtightness in new construction.

companies.name: Aeroseal
companies.what: Aerosolized sealant (LBNL/UC Davis-licensed) that pressurizes ducts (Aeroseal) or whole envelopes (AeroBarrier) and seals leaks from the inside, reaching passive-house airtightness in hours.
companies.signal: $67M Series B (2023) led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Climate Investment; 300,000+ homes sealed, 1,500+ dealers in 90+ countries.

companies.name: SIGA
companies.what: Swiss family firm making high-performance airtightness tapes, membranes and adhesives used in passive-house construction.
companies.signal: Staple of EU and North American high-performance building.

companies.name: Pro Clima (MOLL)
companies.what: INTELLO smart vapor-retarder membranes and complete airtight-system components.
companies.signal: German airtightness pioneer with decades in market.

companies.name: Huber Engineered Woods
companies.what: ZIP System sheathing integrates the structural panel, water-resistive barrier and taped air barrier in one product, displacing housewrap.
companies.signal: Dominant US new-build air-barrier system; J.M. Huber subsidiary.

companies.name: 3M
companies.what: Flashing and air-sealing tapes (8067 All Weather) and air-barrier membranes for residential and commercial envelopes.
companies.signal: Diversified materials incumbent.

companies.name: Henry (Carlisle)
companies.what: Blueskin self-adhered air/water barrier membranes for commercial and residential walls.
companies.signal: Acquired by Carlisle Companies for $1.575B in 2021.

variations.white_space: Aerosolized interior sealing is effectively a one-company category — Aeroseal holds the LBNL-lineage technology with no scaled competitor; automated or robot-applied sealing for the labor-starved retrofit market is open ground.

variations.name: Weatherization diagnostics, tooling and retrofit robotics
variations.description: Blower doors, duct testers, IR cameras, drones and crawl-space robots find and fix where buildings leak, turning weatherization from guesswork into measured performance.

companies.name: Retrotec
companies.what: Blower doors, duct testers and enclosure diagnostic instruments sold worldwide.
companies.signal: Founder retired in 2017; now part of Germany's Wöhler instruments group.

companies.name: The Energy Conservatory
companies.what: Minneapolis Blower Door — the de facto standard for residential airtightness testing — plus DG-1000 gauges and TrueFlow meters.
companies.signal: Decades-standard US diagnostic kit with refreshed product line.

companies.name: Teledyne FLIR
companies.what: Thermal-imaging cameras used to find insulation gaps, thermal bridges and air leaks.
companies.signal: FLIR acquired by Teledyne for ~$8B in 2021; imaging market leader.

companies.name: QEA Tech
companies.what: Drone plus AI building-envelope audits that quantify heat loss per facade element and generate ROI-ranked retrofit roadmaps.
companies.signal: Up to C$4.2M in NRC IRAP support for its patented envelope-audit technology.

companies.name: Lamarr.AI
companies.what: Georgia Tech/MIT/Syracuse spinout automating envelope diagnostics with autonomous drone thermography and AI defect analytics.
companies.signal: $1.1M pre-seed (Hazelview Ventures et al.); global early deployments.

companies.name: Q-Bot
companies.what: Robots that crawl under suspended floors and spray-apply underfloor insulation without lifting floorboards.
companies.signal: £3.5M (2023) plus £1.6M follow-on; 3,000+ UK homes insulated; only BBA-certified robotic underfloor installer.

companies.name: Build Test Solutions
companies.what: UK maker of the Pulse low-pressure airtightness tester and SmartHTC measured whole-house heat-loss metric.
companies.signal: Adopted within UK building-regulation and retrofit measurement schemes.

variations.white_space: Test hardware is a 40-year-old duopoly (Retrotec/TEC); the open ground is the software layer — cheap, automated measured-performance verification (drone thermography, smart-meter-derived heat-loss coefficients) that lets lenders and utilities underwrite retrofit outcomes at portfolio scale.

variations.name: Exterior continuous insulation and overclad products
variations.description: Rigid boards and EIFS systems wrapped outside the structure eliminate thermal bridging through studs — now required by stretch energy codes — using polyiso, phenolic, mineral wool or wood fiber.

companies.name: Kingspan
companies.what: Kooltherm phenolic boards and QuadCore panels for high-R thin exterior continuous insulation.
companies.signal: Multi-billion-euro global insulation leader; also majority owner of Steico for bio-based CI.

companies.name: Sto
companies.what: StoTherm ci exterior insulation and finish systems (EIFS) combining CI, air barrier and finish in one assembly.
companies.signal: Global EIFS leader with US manufacturing.

companies.name: Dryvit (Tremco CPG)
companies.what: Outsulation EIFS systems, among the most-installed exterior insulation claddings in North America.
companies.signal: Part of RPM's Tremco Construction Products Group since 2021.

companies.name: Carlisle (Hunter Panels)
companies.what: Xci polyiso continuous-insulation panels for walls plus integrated WIP air-barrier accessories.
companies.signal: Carlisle Weatherproofing Technologies portfolio company.

companies.name: Atlas Roofing
companies.what: EnergyShield polyiso wall CI boards for residential and commercial overclads.
companies.signal: Family-owned (Hood Companies) US manufacturer.

companies.name: ROCKWOOL
companies.what: Comfortboard rigid mineral-wool exterior CI — fire-safe and vapor-open alternative to foam.
companies.signal: Global stone-wool leader pushing CI in North American codes.

variations.name: Prefabricated panelized deep-retrofit envelopes (Energiesprong-style)
variations.description: Laser-scan a building, factory-build insulated facade and roof cassettes with windows and ventilation already integrated, and clip them onto occupied apartment blocks in days — industrializing deep energy retrofits.

companies.name: Energiesprong
companies.what: Dutch-origin market-development program that standardized net-zero serial retrofits (prefab envelope plus plug-in HVAC pods) and exported the model to DE/FR/UK/US.
companies.signal: Thousands of Dutch units retrofitted; replicated in 5+ countries with dena and national agencies.

companies.name: Ecoworks
companies.what: German serial-retrofit integrator: digital twin to factory-built insulated facade elements with windows and ventilation pre-installed, bringing buildings to net-zero (EH55) standard.
companies.signal: €23M raised March 2026 (Blackhorn Ventures et al.) to deliver Germany's largest serial renovation — 192 apartments across 12 buildings in Hagen.

companies.name: RENOWATE
companies.what: LEG Immobilien + Rhomberg Bau joint venture (founded 2021) using laser-scanned digital twins and prefab facade end-sections to renovate multifamily blocks with tenants in place.
companies.signal: Projects across the DACH region including the Mönchengladbach 'Reallabor'.

variations.white_space: Per-dwelling costs (~€60-100k) still depend on KfW-class subsidies and standardized social-housing stock, so players cluster in NL/DE; no one has industrialized this in the US despite DOE's Advanced Building Construction push — a US integrator pairing prefab overclads with IRA/state retrofit money is wide open.

variations.name: Cool roofs and reflective roofing (incumbent products)
variations.description: White or solar-reflective membranes, shingles, coatings and pavements reject solar gain, cutting cooling loads 10-20% and urban heat-island temperatures — already code-mandated in hot US climate zones.

companies.name: GAF
companies.what: North America's largest roofing maker: cool-rated shingles and TPO plus the Cool Community urban-heat project and StreetBond reflective pavement coating (Time Best Inventions 2022).
companies.signal: Standard Industries unit; Pacoima, LA pilot measured 8-14°F cooler surfaces.

companies.name: Carlisle SynTec
companies.what: White reflective TPO/EPDM single-ply roofing membranes for commercial roofs.
companies.signal: One of the largest US commercial single-ply suppliers.

companies.name: Sika
companies.what: Sarnafil reflective membranes and Sikalastic liquid-applied cool-roof coatings.
companies.signal: Swiss construction-chemicals major with global roofing share.

companies.name: Holcim (Elevate)
companies.what: Former Firestone Building Products; reflective TPO membranes and polyiso under Holcim's roofing/envelope push.
companies.signal: Core of Holcim's multi-billion-dollar US roofing acquisitions since 2021.

variations.name: Passive radiative-cooling coatings and films
variations.description: Metamaterial films and ultra-white paints reflect ~95-98% of sunlight and radiate heat out through the atmosphere's 8-13µm window, cooling surfaces below ambient with zero electricity — a step beyond conventional cool roofs.

companies.name: SkyCool Systems
companies.what: Stanford spinout whose rooftop panels and films cool below ambient to pre-cool refrigeration condensers and HVAC in grocery and industrial buildings.
companies.signal: 2025 revenue $3.3M (10x YoY) with $4.2M contracted backlog; raising $10-15M Series A; CEC-proposed $1.8M grant for a 100,000 sq ft roof demonstration.

companies.name: i2Cool
companies.what: City University of Hong Kong spinout selling electricity-free cooling paints, coatings and films inspired by Saharan silver ants (>95% solar reflection).
companies.signal: Deployments including a stadium pilot showing ~13°C surface reduction; expanding across Asia and the Middle East.

companies.name: SPACECOOL
companies.what: Tokyo-based maker of a radiative-cooling membrane/film with >95% solar reflectivity and 95% atmospheric-window emissivity for warehouses, tents and infrastructure.
companies.signal: Backed by Mitsubishi HC Capital, SPARX, JR East Start Up and other Japanese corporates.

companies.name: Planck Energies
companies.what: Northeastern University spinout formulating ultra-white passive-cooling paints, working with 3M on sprayable roof products for warehouses and reefer trucks.
companies.signal: University Spark Fund-backed; field tests show ≥5°C indoor drops; pre-commercial.

companies.name: 3M
companies.what: Developing passive radiative cooling films and partnering with startups on cooling paint formulations.
companies.signal: Diversified materials incumbent entering via films and partnerships.

companies.name: Radi-Cool
companies.what: Commercializes CU Boulder-origin glass-bead metamaterial radiative-cooling film, with deployments concentrated in China.
companies.signal: Industrial deployments in Asia; limited verifiable Western presence.

variations.white_space: Physics is proven but durability, dirt pickup and $/m² are not solved at commodity scale; the field is seed-stage startups while coatings majors move slowly — Purdue's record 98.1%-reflective barium-sulfate paint is still in tech transfer, so a mass-market cooling paint pushed through Sherwin-Williams/PPG-class distribution is the opening.

variations.name: Green roofs and vegetated envelopes
variations.description: Engineered soil-and-plant assemblies on roofs insulate, cut peak cooling, retain stormwater and reduce urban heat — a mature, mandate-driven industry in Europe now growing in North America.

companies.name: ZinCo
companies.what: German pioneer of engineered green-roof build-ups (drainage/retention layers, solar-plus-green combinations) sold in 50+ countries.
companies.signal: Decades-long category leader.

companies.name: Optigrün (Optigreen)
companies.what: German market leader in green and blue 'retention roof' systems engineered for stormwater control.
companies.signal: Top European market share.

companies.name: Sempergreen
companies.what: Dutch grower of pre-vegetated sedum blankets and living-wall systems with global distribution.
companies.signal: Q1 2024 strategic partnership with LiveRoof to co-develop modular systems for the US.

companies.name: LiveRoof
companies.what: US patented modular pre-grown living-roof tray system installed full-grown.
companies.signal: Partnered with Sempergreen (2024) to expand US modular green-roof reach.

companies.name: Omni Ecosystems
companies.what: Chicago firm whose ultralight engineered growing media lets ordinary roof structures carry biodiverse intensive meadows.
companies.signal: US projects including high-profile commercial HQs.

companies.name: American Hydrotech (Sika)
companies.what: Garden Roof hot-applied membrane plus vegetated assembly, a longtime US specifier favorite.
companies.signal: Acquired by Sika in 2017; continues under Sika's roofing portfolio.

variations.name: Conventional fiberglass and mineral wool with low-carbon manufacturing
variations.description: Fiberglass and stone wool remain the workhorse envelope insulation worldwide, and the incumbents are decarbonizing it — electrifying melters, raising recycled content and switching to bio-based binders — which matters because their volumes dwarf every alternative material combined.

companies.name: Owens Corning
companies.what: World's largest fiberglass insulation maker; PINK Next Gen fiberglass with high recycled glass content and published EPDs.
companies.signal: NYSE: OC, ~$11B revenue with a multi-billion-dollar insulation segment.

companies.name: Knauf Insulation
companies.what: Glass wool with bio-based ECOSE binder; building a £172M low-carbon rock-mineral-wool plant in the UK and acquired an electric-melt plant in Uzbekistan (Oct 2024).
companies.signal: Major capex committed to electric melting and low-embodied-carbon lines.

companies.name: ROCKWOOL
companies.what: Global stone-wool leader electrifying its melting process — the company's biggest decarbonization lever — with electric lines in Scandinavia and new plants planned.
companies.signal: €389M in decarbonization investments approved in 2025, including new electric production lines and PPAs in Poland and Spain.

companies.name: Saint-Gobain
companies.what: Isover glass wool and CertainTeed North America; piloting electric glass-wool furnaces and expanding via its multi-billion-dollar CSR (Australia) acquisition in 2024.
companies.signal: €45B+ construction-materials major with stated 2050 net-zero roadmap.

companies.name: Johns Manville
companies.what: Berkshire Hathaway-owned maker of fiberglass and mineral wool insulation plus commercial roofing.
companies.signal: Top-four North American insulation producer.
